newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG WINS SLALOM TO INCREASE WORLD CUP LEAD.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG WINS SLALOM TO INCREASE WORLD CUP LEAD.

text.p: Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg kept her Scandinavian cool in demanding conditions on Saturday, to win a women's slalom and increase her lead in the overall World Cup standings.
The 26-year-old now has 718 overall points -- 155 more than Germany's defending title-holder Katja Seizinger, who impressed rivals with ninth place in her first slalom of the winter.
But while Seizinger still favours the speed disciplines, Wiberg has developed into an all-round skier capable of winning in downhill and slalom.
This season, Wiberg has claimed the super-giant slalom in Lake Louise and the first of back-to-back slaloms in Semmering last week, for a total of 15 career World Cup victories.
She was also second in a super-G in Vail and at the season's opening slaloms at Park City and Crans Montana, as well as finishing third in a downhill at Lake Louise.

On Saturday, Wiberg underlined her position as one of the leading figures in slalom this season. Fastest in the first run, she was unruffled by deteriorating conditions and falling snow on the Radvanje piste.

The reigning slalom world champion clocked fastest times in both runs for a best aggregate time of one minute 44.55 seconds, on a hill which claimed many prominent victims including Austrian-born Claudia Riegler, who races for New Zealand and has won two slaloms this winter.
But Wiberg said she would not yet dare dream about the coveted overall title.
"It is far too early to start talking about the overall," said Wiberg, who lives in Monaco.
"I take each race at a time. I will start thinking about the overall after the world championships (in February in Sestriere)," added the triple world and twice Olympic champion.
Local heroine Urska Hrovat recorded her best result of the winter by taking second place on Saturday in 1:45.32.
Despite failing to repeat her victory at Maribor from 1994, she delighted home crowds in the finish area and rolled in the snow in triumph.
Italy's Lara Magoni improved from a first run seventh to overall third with 1:46.46 -- her best World Cup performance.
